items.title: Punjab And Haryana Spar Over Who Is Really Tackling Stubble Burning
points: The political battle over Delhi's worsening air pollution has taken a fresh turn, with the BJP-led Haryana government responding to AAP's challenge over stubble burning by highlighting its incentive-based strategy to prevent farm fires.

The latest exchange follows Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema's sharp attack on the BJP, in which he questioned why Punjab was being repeatedly blamed for Delhi's pollution while farm fires in Haryana, also an agricultural state, were allegedly…
Under its Parali Protsahan Yojana, the Haryana government is offering farmers an incentive of Rs 1,200 per acre for the effective utilisation of crop-residue management machinery.
According to Punjab Pollution Control Board data, the state recorded 3,144 farm-fire incidents between September 15 and November 6, 2026.
Tarn Taran accounted for the highest number at 611, followed by Ferozepur with 410, Sangrur with 281, Bathinda with 262 and Amritsar with 231.

items.title: Punjab Gangster, Wanted For Killings And Extortion, Deported From Ethiopia
points: In a major breakthrough against organised crime, the Punjab Police has secured the deportation of Gurwinder alias Afridi, a key kingpin of the Doni Bal-Prabh Dassuwal gang, from Ethiopia after a 10-month-long international manhunt under Operation SHAHID.

The operation was carried out by the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF), Punjab, in coordination with the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC) of Counter Intelligence, Punjab, with support from central agencies.

According to preliminary investigations, Gurwinder alias Afridi was allegedly operating from abroad and directing targeted killings, extortion-related firing incidents and other organised criminal activities in Punjab.
The Punjab Government had announced a reward of Rs 5 lakh for information leading to his arrest, highlighting the priority attached to tracking down the fugitive.
Preliminary investigation reveals that the accused was allegedly directing targeted killings, extortion-related firing incidents and organised criminal activities in Punjab from abroad.
The Punjab Government had announced a reward of ₹5 lakh on the information leading to his arrest.

items.title: HT Morning News Brief November 8: Delhi’s worst Diwali eve air in 10 years; Israel Prez picks Netanyahu rival Eisenkot, and more
points: Delhi woke up to Diwali on Sunday after recording its most polluted festival eve in a decade.
The city's air quality index (AQI) stood at 369 at 4 pm on Saturday, placing it in the ‘very poor’ category on the Central Pollution Control Board’s (CPCB) 0-500 scale.
This was the highest AQI recorded on the day before Diwali since 2016, when it touched 404.

The embassy of India in Tehran celebrated Diwali with members of the Indian and Iranian communities, along with diplomats, bringing together people to mark the festival of lights and experience the country’s rich cultural traditions.

items.title: Fortnite Finally Reveals Drop Rates of Pirate Shop Token
points: After days of anticipation and community outrage behind finding the elusive Pirate Shop Token in Fortnite, Epic Games has finally dropped the curtain on its drop rate and how the entire RNG dynamics work this mini-season.
According to Epic, each player has a fair and equal chance to snag the Pirate Shop Token in a Fortnite match, however, the odds stand at a bizarre 1 in 137,500 chance of finding it.

items.title: Punjab Government To Offer Free Civil Services Coaching To 1,000 College Students
points: The Punjab government will provide free online coaching for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) Civil Services and Punjab Civil Services (PCS) examinations to 1,000 college students.
The initiative is aimed at helping students prepare for civil services examinations without spending money on expensive coaching programmes or travelling to big cities.
According to PTI, an official statement, 750 students from government colleges and 250 from private colleges will be selected for the programme.
Education Minister Harjot Bains is leading the initiative.
He added that the Punjab Sikhiya Kranti was not just about improving classrooms but also about creating better opportunities for students.

The programme will include: Education Minister Harjot Bains said students from villages and small towns would get access to structured preparation and guidance similar to what is available at major coaching centres.
The programme will cover 1,000 selected students from government and private colleges across Punjab.
Of these, 750 seats will be for government college students, while 250 will be reserved for students from private colleges.

items.title: Missing Woman's Decomposed Body Found In Gunny Bag Near Guwahati Temple
points: The body of a woman who had gone missing nearly 12 days ago was found in a gunny bag near Ganesh Temple in Guwahati's Khanapara, Assam.
The body was recovered at around 11.15 am on Saturday after some local residents noticed what appeared to be human legs protruding from a spot near the temple.
A team from Dispur Police Station rushed to the location and initiated an investigation.
The 38-year-old woman was later identified as a resident of Koinadhora.
The remains were subsequently shifted to Gauhati Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) for a post-mortem examination to establish the cause and approximate time of death.
The woman had reportedly been untraceable for nearly 12 days.
Following her disappearance, her family approached Basistha Police Station and lodged a missing-person complaint.
Investigators are examining how she went missing and how her body ended up near the Khanapara temple.

items.title: Punjab Police brings back wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi from Ethiopia
points: Punjab Police on Sunday brought wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi back to India from Ethiopia.
He landed at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport early in the morning and is being escorted to Punjab by a team of the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF).
A resident of Tut village in Tarn Taran district, Afridi carries a reward of ₹5 lakh announced by the Punjab government.
Police sources described the operation as the first instance of Punjab Police securing the return of a fugitive from an African country.
Afridi's name surfaced in the investigation into the August 31, 2022, attack on a church in Thakkarpura village of Tarn Taran.
In June 2024, Amritsar Rural Police arrested Jaswinder Singh alias Munshi, describing him as a key accused in the case.
Afridi was also named in a 2021 FIR registered at Sadar Patti police station in Tarn Taran under Sections 380 and 457 of the IPC, relating to theft and house-breaking, and Section 25 of the Arms Act.

items.title: HC restrains unauthorised use of Amitabh’s name, likeness
points: The Delhi high court has permanently protected the personality rights of veteran Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan, restraining entities from using his name, image, voice or other aspects of his persona without his consent.

A bench of justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav in his November 5 order, decreed the suit filed by Bachchan in 2022 after being informed that he had entered into settlements with four entities, which acknowledged his publicity rights and right to privacy.

As part of the settlement, one individual informed the court that he had taken steps to remove the mobile application titled Amitabh Bachchan Video Call, while the other said that it had discontinued publication of its General Knowledge Quizbook, which…
One individual submitted that it had stopped selling posters bearing Bachchan’s image, name and likeness.
Meanwhile, another informed the court that he had deleted the domain name amitabhbachchan.in in November 2022 and had not derived any monetary benefit from it.

items.title: Acquitted, but disarmed: SC orders cops to return bodyguard’s revolver
points: Mohammad Jamal Mohammad Yunus learnt this the hard way when the police seized his licensed revolver in 2012 in a criminal case, leaving him unable to find work in the very profession he depended on to feed his family.

Linking the prolonged deprivation of the weapon to its impact on his livelihood, a bench of justices Vikram Nath, R Mahadevan and Aparesh Kumar Singh directed Maharashtra to return it within eight weeks, subject to compliance with the applicable…
The bench directed the state to take necessary steps to hand over the revolver to Yunus within eight weeks, subject to compliance with the applicable requirements under the Arms Act, 1959.

Yunus’s revolver was seized in 2012 during the investigation of an FIR registered at Bazar Peth police station in Jalgaon under provisions relating to attempt to murder, abetment and destruction of evidence, as well as the Arms Act.

items.title: MPSC Group-C Recruitment 2026: Vacancies Increased To 16,717, Exam On January 24
points: The Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) has increased the vacancies for the Maharashtra Group-C Services Combined Preliminary Examination 2026 from 5,707 to 16,717.
With this revision, a total of 11,010 additional posts have been added to the recruitment drive.
The exam, which was earlier scheduled for January 3, 2027, will now be held on January 24, 2027.
The revised vacancy count will allow more candidates to apply for various Group-C government positions in Maharashtra.
Following the addition of new posts and cadres, MPSC will reopen the application window from November 13 to November 27, 2026.
The relaxation follows a Government Resolution issued by the General Administration Department on November 5, 2026.

MPSC has also revised the examination scheme to include 21 additional cadres in the Maharashtra Group-C Services Combined Examination.The commission had initially released the examination scheme on May 20, 2026, covering six cadres.
Later, it received recruitment requests for 21 more cadres following a Government Resolution issued by the General Administration Department on May 5, 2026.

FSSAI led an intensive nationwide inspection drive across States and UTs.

This calendar year, the FSSAI has stepped up enforcement actions against food business operators and e-commerce companies to ensure safe food for consumers.

items.title: Mint Explainer: Will Sebi’s new rules on currency derivatives help the falling rupee?
points: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has introduced a new set of norms to curb the flow in rupee-related currency derivatives transactions.

The move, which follows a recent Reserve Bank of India (RBI) circular, is expected to reduce pressure on the rupee at a time when geopolitical tensions and market instability have caused the currency to depreciate.

Under Sebi’s revised rules, domestic investors and foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) can hold long or short rupee-denominated currency positions of up to $5 million across all stock exchanges combined, without needing to prove an underlying investment…
The revised rules also prescribe specific conditions for FPIs: their short positions across all contracts in foreign currency-rupee pairs cannot exceed $5 million across exchanges.
The move follows RBI’s circular issued on 10 October, which slashed the threshold for taking positions without establishing an underlying exposure from $100 million to $5 million.

items.title: Singapore-based senior IT executive shot dead over parking dispute in Faridabad
points: The police have arrested the accused, identified as Mohan Sharma, a real estate agent who lived on the third floor of the same multi-storey building in Sector 21C where the victim resided with his family.
The victim, Paramjith Dhankhar, had returned from Singapore two days ago to attend a family wedding and celebrate Deepavali with his family.

According to the complaint filed by his 19-year-old son, Shaurya, the accused rang the doorbell of their flat around 8.30 p.m. and asked Mr. Dhankhar, who had returned from the gym a few minutes earlier, to come downstairs and move his car.
Shaurya also accompanied his father to the parking area.
An argument reportedly broke out between the two men, following which Mr. Sharma allegedly pulled out a pistol and fired several rounds at Mr. Dhankhar.
“About 14-15 rounds were fired, of which eight or nine reportedly hit the victim.
His son, who was present at the spot, escaped unhurt,” said Surajkund police station SHO Inspector Pahlad.

items.title: PM Modi extends Diwali wishes, to celebrate festival with jawans today
points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday extended Diwali greetings to the people across the country, wishing everyone on the occasion of the festival of lights.
He reiterated his tradition of celebrating Diwali with jawans, continuing his annual gesture of spending the festival with armed forces personnel.

On Saturday, PM Modi had extended Diwali greetings to the nation through a video message, highlighting the festival as a symbol of light’s triumph over darkness and expressing hope for happiness, peace and prosperity for all citizens.
In a 50-second video message shared on social media platforms including X, Modi appeared in traditional attire with a tilak and addressed people directly, extending his greetings on the festival.

Offering “very best wishes” to everyone, he prayed that the festival and the “days ahead remain filled with happiness, peace and prosperity.” The Prime Minister also spoke about his personal practice of celebrating Diwali with great enthusiasm.
PM Modi’s annual visits to military locations on Diwali have become a consistent feature of his tenure since 2014.
